interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: Root SSH with password or key at creation, systemd inside the container, Docker allowed, panel reinstall. Login through Discord OAuth.
chaining: A throwaway IPv6 container with a dedicated public address is the cheapest way to test an inbound service or hold a trickle of state for a week. It composes badly with anything long-running: the 7-day clock and the 35% CPU throttle rule out indexing and builds.

limits.value: the free period is 7 days and must be renewed by hand at most once every 24 hours; an unrenewed VPS is auto-suspended
one free container per account is implied by the FAQ's singular 'your VPS' but is not stated as a number anywhere read

limits_note: Container lifetime is seven days with manual renewal available once every 24 hours; unattended containers suspend after seven days. Hardware is consumer-grade without an availability guarantee.
binding_note: a 7-day clock that resets only when a human renews is the first thing that fails: any lapse in renewal past 7 days suspends the machine

identity_cost.detail: No card and no hold: the home page says 'no card required just Discord', and the FAQ says 'no trial, no card required'. Sign-in is through Clerk (clerk.openworld.eu.org) on the /login page, whose form is a single 'Sign in' button and carries no card, phone or document field; the page footer credits the builder. Whether the Clerk instance offers an email-only sign-up or requires a social account was not established: the button is rendered disabled until the Clerk JavaScript loads, so the flow could not be read from the markup.

superseded.notes: The site publishes no spec table at all, so the shape here comes from the operator's LowEndTalk post and is dated to that post rather than to the site. Two third-party renewable scripts exist, which is a good sign the offer is live and a bad sign about how the renewal is experienced. The 50 GB a week figure is the only egress number and it comes from the forum post, not the site; the site itself publishes no bandwidth figure. Throttle after the cap is 1 Mbit/s rather than a cut-off. This is the weakest of the three sibling offers on hosting quality and the strongest on reachability, because it needs nothing but Discord.

confidence_note: Retention, networking, root SSH access, and payment requirements are quoted from first-party documentation. Hardware shape derives from reported third-party benchmarks. Account creation was not performed; published numbers are unmeasured against live endpoints.
